ei.title: The Limits of Digital Political Movements
ei.subject: 수능특강

fullPassage: Over the past twenty years, with the arrival of digital politics, social and political protest movements have changed and become ever more prominent through what the sociologist Manuel Castells has called Networks of Outrage and Hope. We now have a swirling world of 'online activism', digital rebellion, information politics and People's Platforms. Smartphones and social networking now provide a more fluid, leaderless, participatory activism that arises more spontaneously. The early examples like the Occupy Movement (2011), the Arab Spring in Egypt (2010), the Umbrella Movement in Hong Kong (2014, 2019), the Gezi Park Movement in Turkey (2013), and the Pussy Riots in Russia (2011) galvanized large numbers of people and attracted world attention. While some suggest that these new politics are enhancing democracy, others maintain that they do not really challenge the dominant power groups. Looking back, most of them have proved unsuccessful, clamped down upon by the state. There seems a limit to the power of new social movements.

det.korean: ③ enhanced → enhancing: are enhancing (진행형 능동태)

det.korean: ① participatorily → participatory: a more fluid, leaderless, participatory activism에서 명사 activism을 수식하는 형용사 필요

❌ ① participatorily: fluid, leaderless와 병렬로 activism을 수식하는 형용사 자리. 부사형 participatorily는 부적절. ←정답

✅ ② attracted: galvanized와 and로 병렬된 과거동사 적절.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ③ discouraged(의욕을 꺾었다) → galvanized(자극하여 행동하게 했다): 많은 사람을 자극하여 세계의 관심을 끌었다는 문맥
det.analysis:
✅ ① prominent (두드러진): 시위 운동이 더 prominent해졌다는 문맥에 적절.

✅ ② spontaneously (자발적으로): 더 자발적으로 발생한다는 문맥에 적절.

❌ ③ discouraged (의욕을 꺾었다): 원문은 galvanized(자극하여 행동하게 했다). 대규모 인원을 동원하고 세계의 관심을 끌었으므로 discouraged는 문맥과 반대. ←정답

✅ ④ unsuccessful (실패한): 대부분 실패로 판명되었다는 문맥에 적절.
det.tip: galvanize = 자극하여 행동하게 하다 ↔ discourage = 의욕을 꺾다

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ② concede(인정하다) → maintain(주장하다): 일부는 민주주의를 강화한다고 제안하고, 다른 이들은 지배 권력에 진정한 도전이 되지 못한다고 '주장한다'는 대조 맥락
det.analysis:
✅ ① swirling (소용돌이치는): 온라인 활동주의의 역동적 세계를 묘사하는 데 적절.

❌ ② concede (인정하다): 원문은 maintain(주장하다). some suggest ~ enhancing democracy vs. others maintain ~ not challenge. 대조적 주장을 '인정하다'가 아니라 '주장하다'로 표현하는 것이 문맥상 적절. concede는 상대 입장을 양보/인정한다는 뜻으로 대조 구문에 부적절. ←정답

✅ ③ challenge (도전하다): 지배 권력에 도전하지 못한다는 문맥에 적절.

✅ ④ limit (한계): 새로운 사회운동의 힘에 한계가 있다는 문맥에 적절.
det.tip: maintain = 주장하다 (assert, claim) ↔ concede = 인정하다/양보하다

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 빈칸에 ever more prominent(점점 더 두드러진)가 적절
det.analysis:
❌ ① gradually marginalized (점차 주변화된): 디지털 정치의 도래로 시위 운동이 변화하고 두드러졌다는 문맥과 반대.

✅ ② ever more prominent (점점 더 두드러진): 변화하고 더 두드러졌다는 원문 맥락에 부합. ←정답

det.korean: 빈칸에 the dominant power groups(지배적인 권력 집단)가 적절

questions.passage: Over the past twenty years, with the arrival of digital politics, social and political protest movements have changed and become ever more prominent through what the sociologist Manuel Castells has called <u>Networks of Outrage and Hope</u>. We now have a swirling world of 'online activism', digital rebellion, information politics and People's Platforms. Smartphones and social networking now provide a more fluid, leaderless, participatory activism that arises more spontaneously. The early examples like the Occupy Movement (2011), the Arab Spring in Egypt (2010), the Umbrella Movement in Hong Kong (2014, 2019), the Gezi Park Movement in Turkey (2013), and the Pussy Riots in Russia (2011) galvanized large numbers of people and attracted world attention. While some suggest that these new politics are enhancing democracy, others maintain that they do not really challenge the dominant power groups. Looking back, most of them have proved unsuccessful, clamped down upon by the state. There seems a limit to the power of new social movements.
